items.title: Alvin Alcorn and Eddie Marrero Interview, 1979-12-04
items.q: Papa was 16 and quit and turned the band over to Sam Morgan... Sam Morgan took the band.

ctx.s: Alvin Alcorn (co-interviewee / Marrero family member, NOT interviewer)

ctx.x: When you were 16, you gave up then. Papa was 16 and quit and turned the band over to Sam Morgan. Yes, sir. That same Sam Morgan, see, that. Well, Sam Morgan took the band. So, he got to be famous, Sam Morgan. But when Papa died, Sam Morgan took over all the dad.

ctx.s: Alvin Alcorn (co-interviewee / Marrero family member, NOT interviewer)
ctx.x: And who was that man? Huh? He used to do with Daddy. They used to call Wooden Joe.

items.title: Eddie Marrero Interview, 1961-10-11
items.q: Did you say you played in the Morgan band, the Sam Morgan... [INTERVIEWEE] Well, yeah, when I walk in the dance.

ctx.x: He's a third corner player. My daddy's friend. He was the third and the next to the last. The last man was Sam Morgan. Sam Morgan was the last.
I knew Bung White well when he came back.

items.title: Eddie Marrero Interview, 1961-10-11
items.q: He's one of the youngest Morgan brothers. He'd come after all of them.

ctx.x: Is that right? I didn't see him.
Yeah, he was down here about two years ago. He's one of the youngest Morgan brothers. He'd come after all of them. Yeah.
Did you say you played in the Morgan band, the Sam Morgan, like did you ever take a substitute or anything for Jim Little, or he was usually the bass player?
